message.content:
**Traffic Laws Overview – State of Texas** | Topic | Key Provisions | |-------|----------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Rural interstate/US‑Highways: 75–85 mph (often 70 mph).
• Urban/interstates: 55–65 mph.
• County roads: 35–45 mph unless posted otherwise.
• “No‑limit” zones exist only on some interstates; all other roads have posted limits. | | **Seat Belt Law** | All occupants must wear seat belts while vehicle is moving. Failure results in a $50 fine plus possible court costs. | | **Cell Phone Use** | • Handheld cell phones prohibited while driving (unless using hands‑free).
• Texting while driving is illegal under §545.021(1)(b) (no texting with both hands free). | | **Alcohol / Drug Impairment** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) ≥0.08 % constitutes DUI.
• Lower BAC thresholds apply to commercial drivers (≥0.04 %) and new drivers (<18 years old).
• Penalties include fines ($500+), license suspension, mandatory education programs, and potential jail time. | | **Odometer Fraud** | Tampering with odometer readings is a felony punishable up to 2 years imprisonment and/or $10k fine. | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • At uncontrolled intersections, vehicles approaching from the right yield first.
• Stop signs require full stop before proceeding.
• Yield to pedestrians crossing crosswalks even if no sign present. | | **School Bus Regulations** | Vehicles must stop when school buses display flashing red lights and open doors. Drivers may not pass until lights cease and doors close. | | **Pedestrian Rights** | Pedestrians always have priority at marked crosswalks. In unmarked areas, they still have right‑of‑way where visibility allows safe passage. | | **Lane Discipline** | • Lane changes without signaling within 100 feet of intersection are unlawful.
• Passing on the left is allowed only on multi-lane roads and when overtaken vehicle is turning right. | | **Parking Restrictions** | Parking bans near fire hydrants, driveways, railroad crossings, and curbside loading/unloading zones are strictly enforced. | | **Points System** | Accumulating 12 points in two consecutive years leads to automatic driver’s licence revocation. Points vary per offense (e.g., speeding >20 mph over limit = 5 pts). | ### How Violations Are Enforced * **Tickets:** Issued by police officers or county sheriffs. Must be paid within 30 days or appear in court. * **Court Process:** Minor infractions often resolved via citation payment or online portal. Major offenses (DUI, reckless driving) lead to arraignment. * **Fines & Fees:** Vary by jurisdiction—county courts set base amounts; additional fees added for administrative processing. ### Resources for Detailed Information | Resource | What It Offers | |----------|---------------| | **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV)** | Licensing info, penalty schedules, electronic ticket payments. | | **Texas Transportation Code** | Full statutory text governing road usage. Available online through state legislature site. | | **County Sheriff’s Office Websites** | Local ordinances, parking regulations, and public safety notices. | | **Legal Aid Organizations** | Free consultations for those facing serious charges (e.g., DUI). | --- #### Quick Reference Cheat Sheet ``` [ ] Wear seatbelt → $50 fine + court cost [ ] Hands-free cellphone ONLY [ ] Speed ≤ posted limit (rural 70–80 mph, urban 55–65 mph) [ ] Stop for school bus w/flashing red light [ ] Keep 200 ft distance when passing slower vehicle [ ] Do NOT park within 15 ft of driveway entrance [ ] If you get a ticket, pay within 30 days OR contest in court ``` Feel free to ask if you'd like deeper details on any specific area (speed limits in your city, how to appeal a ticket, etc.).
